content:
Cia declassified memo provides the author's personal understanding of scalar waves (also called non-Hertzian or Tesla-type waves in fringe literature). It discusses them as hypothetical non-electromagnetic (non-EM) waves with unusual propagation properties.

Main points from the memo:

Definition and Nature

Scalar waves are described as potential non-EM waves that differ from conventional electromagnetic waves. They supposedly involve longitudinal rather than transverse wave propagation (in contrast to normal EM waves).

Historical/Fringe References

The author references several figures known in alternative science circles:

Nikola Tesla — as the original conceptual source

T. E. Bearden (Tom Bearden) — specifically mentions his "Fer-de-Lance" briefing on alleged Soviet scalar weapons

Other implied or related researchers in scalar/zero-point/Tesla-tech fields

Claimed Properties  

Unconventional wave propagation (possibly through solid matter or over long distances with little attenuation)

Potential for military applications (weapons, communications, etc.)

Links to Soviet research programs (common Cold War-era concern at the time)

"In summary, scalar waves refer to non-EM waves with the potential for unconventional wave propagation."
